name: Luciano Manhães de Andrade Filho
title: Prof. Dr.
bio: Full Professor at UFJF and Team Leader of the UFJF group at CERN/ATLAS. He holds a B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering (UERJ, 2001), an M.Sc. in Scientific Instrumentation (CBPF, 2004, sandwich at CERN/LHCb), and a Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering (UFRJ/COPPE, 2009, sandwich at CERN/ATLAS), complemented by two post-doctorates — one in PLC communications at UFJF (2009) and another in Nuclear Instrumentation at CERN (2021). He is the Coordinator of the NIPS-CERN Lab and a member of the INCT CERN-Brasil (Instituto Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia para Física de Altas Energias com o CERN). His expertise spans signal processing for calorimetry, FPGA-based systems, and machine learning applied to particle detectors. Web of Science: 1,256 works · 67,244 citations · h-index 118. Scopus: 1,207 works · 78,835 citations · h-index 124.

awards.title: Most-Liked Video — SEMIC 2025 ("Macro e Microcosmos: Fractais e a Física de Partículas")

name: Chrysthofer Arthur Amaro Afonso
title: B.Sc. Student
bio: He began his training in the exact sciences, with emphasis on physics, astronomy, and mathematics, through national and international olympiads, in which he earned gold, silver, and bronze medals, and through the OBMEP Scientific Initiation Program conducted by IMPA. This path led him to Electrical Engineering, which he is currently pursuing, with emphasis on Electronic Systems, at the Federal University of Juiz de Fora (UFJF), Brazil. At UFJF, he is part of the NIPS-CERN laboratory, where he carries out undergraduate research, and of the National Institute of Science and Technology (INCT) CERN-Brazil, contributing to support activities for the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) experiments at CERN (Organisation européenne pour la recherche nucléaire), in Geneva, Switzerland. As a FAPEMIG BIC fellow, he leads the project 'Extensions of the Lorenzetti Framework for Three-Dimensional Event Visualization and Free-Running Data Generation for Trigger Studies in Calorimetry'. He also works on processor architecture, reconfigurable hardware, and scientific software within the SAPHO ecosystem, and develops xCGV, a 3D event visualizer aimed at the High-Luminosity phase of the LHC. In parallel, he maintains independent scholarly activity in logic, taking part in international seminars and networks such as the Nordic Online Logic Seminar and the Young Network for Wittgensteinian Philosophy, of which he is a member.

name: Ana Luíza Gonçalves Figueiredo
bio: She joined NIPS-CERN in September 2026 to work on the SIENA project. The image on her tile is her own photograph of the Milky Way.

name: Fábio Cardani Luna
title: Me.
bio: Electrical engineer with a Master's in Electrical Engineering and currently a Ph.D. candidate. Experienced in digital signal processing, digital electronics and FPGA development, applied to high-energy-physics instrumentation in the ATLAS experiment (CERN). Research focuses on real-time signal simulation and processing, with emphasis on hardware digital filters — including floating-point IIR architectures to mitigate quantization errors and improve numerical precision. Skilled in large-scale experimental data analysis with Python and C++ (ROOT), covering .root file processing, histogram generation, statistical studies and detection-system performance evaluation. Interested in embedded systems, DSP and large scientific experiments.

name: Melissa Santos Aguiar
title: Me.
bio: Graduated and Master in Electrical Engineering in the area of ​​Electronic Systems from the Federal University of Juiz de Fora (UFJF). Currently, part of CERN as a Scientific Associate and working as a Technological Development Analyst at the National Synchrotron Light Laboratory (LNLS).

name: Vinicius Pires Diniz de Oliveira
bio: Electrical Engineering student (Telecommunications) at UFJF. Since 2023, a research fellow on the ATLAS/CERN experiment, focused on energy reconstruction and the development and validation of detection systems; since September 2026 he works on HITS, the FPGA simulator of the TileCal readout chain. Previously a Telecommunications specialist, with experience in VoIP, PBX, IPv4/IPv6 networks and large-scale technical support. Served as an academic monitor at UFJF, supporting teaching and practical activities. Was Simulations and Research coordinator for the Supernova Rocketry team, leading computational modeling, aerodynamic simulation and structural integration. Also volunteered at the UFJF Science Center Astronomical Observatory, assisting in scientific outreach and instrument operation.

name: Dabson Ferreira dos Santos
bio: Completed secondary education at the Colégio Militar de Juiz de Fora (2014). Currently a PIBIC fellow at the Federal University of Juiz de Fora.

name: Ana Luiza Bernardes Pereira de Carvalho
bio: B.Sc. student in Electrical Engineering (Robotics and Industrial Automation) at UFJF since 2024; her Lattes lists Electrical Engineering with emphasis on Control and Automation as her area. She joined NIPS-CERN in September 2026 to work on HITS, the FPGA simulator of the TileCal readout chain, with Fábio Luna.

name: Leon Felipe Guedim Millani
bio: B.Sc. student in Electrical Engineering (Power Systems) at UFJF since 2024. He joined NIPS-CERN in September 2026 to work on the impact of phase deviation on online energy reconstruction by pseudoinverse deconvolution for the ATLAS liquid-argon calorimeter, co-advised by Eder Kapisch.

name: Pedro Henrique Sereno Romeu dos Santos
bio: Completed secondary education at Escola Estadual Professor Sousa Nilo (2019). B.Sc. student in Electrical Engineering (Electronic Systems) at UFJF since 2020, with experience in electric, magnetic and electronic circuits. Works on the SAPHO project with Sabrina Amaral, testing the processor on the laboratory's FPGA boards.

name: João Pedro de Souza Salomé
bio: B.Sc. student at UFJF since 2025; his Lattes lists Electrical Engineering with emphasis on Telecommunications as his area. He joined NIPS-CERN in September 2026 to work on CGV, the 3D visualizer of the ATLAS calorimeter.

name: Leandro da Graça Ribeiro
title: Me.
bio: Electrical Engineer with an emphasis on Electronics, currently working at the European Organization for Nuclear Research (CERN). PhD student in Electrical Engineering at the Federal University of Juiz de Fora, focusing on Electronic Systems. He has a technical course in Electronics from Escola Técnica Pandiá Calógeras (2017). He was an intern at the Federal University of Juiz de Fora, where he also completed his undergraduate and master's degrees in Electrical Engineering, with an emphasis on Electronic Systems.

name: Daniela Mendes Nepomuceno
bio: B.Sc. student in Electrical Engineering (Robotics and Industrial Automation) at UFJF since 2023. Member of the PET Elétrica tutorial education programme at UFJF, taking part in teaching, research, extension and project development. She joined NIPS-CERN in September 2026 to work on CGV, the 3D visualizer of the ATLAS calorimeter.

name: Arthur Araújo Martins
bio: Graduating in Electrical Engineering - Electronic Systems from the Federal University of Juiz de Fora (UFJF). Currently, he is developing Scientific Initiation research (VIC) in the project ''Functional Extension and Experimental Evaluation of the SAPHO Autoscalable Processor for Embedded FPGA Applications'', with a focus on software documentation. He has a profile focused on academic leadership and technical volunteering, simultaneously serving as Secretary of the Computer Society (CS) and Power Energy Society (PES) Student Chapters of the IEEE UFJF Student Branch. Interested in Embedded Systems, Technical Documentation Management, FPGA Prototyping. He develops Solar, a toolchain orchestration infrastructure in Rust for development with the SAPHO soft-core processor alongside the AURORA IDE: a core library, Solar-Core, manages a versioned bundle of tools and exposes a stable internal API, with interchangeable interfaces built on top, starting with a CLI. The orchestration targets YANC and the open-source software used to develop and verify SAPHO processors.

name: Heitor Duarte Balthazar
bio: B.Sc. student in Electrical Engineering (Robotics and Industrial Automation) at UFJF since 2023, with main interests in robotics, control and automation. Teaching assistant for Calculus II at UFJF (2025 to 2026). He joined NIPS-CERN in September 2026 to work on energy reconstruction for the ATLAS liquid-argon calorimeter, co-advised by Eder Kapisch.

name: Tiago Aparecido Teixeira
title: Me. Dr.
bio: Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from UFJF and Master in Computer Science from UFV, with a specialization in IT Project Management and a degree in Computer Science. Currently a Systems Analyst at Juiz de Fora City Hall, with academic and professional experience in Data Science, Artificial Intelligence and Computing Systems. As a researcher on the ATLAS experiment (CERN/LHC), worked on online filtering, energy estimation and signal processing under High-Luminosity conditions, implementing deconvolution algorithms and Neural Networks on FPGAs and coarse-grained architectures. Recently expanded to Data Engineering and applied Machine Learning, with bootcamp training and industry work in fintechs and the international real-estate sector, leading predictive-model and Generative AI projects.

name: Sabrina de Oliveira Amaral
bio: B.Sc. student in Electrical Engineering (Electronic Systems) at UFJF and Electromechanics technician from IF Sudeste MG (2017). Professional and academic experience in electro-electronic maintenance, embedded systems (ESP32, C/C++), automation and engineering, with participation in electric-vehicle and renewable-energy projects. Intern at MRS Logística (2023 to 2025) and maintenance apprentice at IMBEL (2020 to 2021). Works with MATLAB, PSIM, AutoCAD and Power BI. She joined NIPS-CERN in September 2026 to implement and test the SAPHO processor on different FPGA boards, advised by Luciano.

name: Ualison Rodrigo Ferreira Dias
title: Me. Dr.
bio: Electrical Engineer (Electronic Systems) focused on Artificial Intelligence, with Master's and Ph.D. from UFJF and a B.Sc. in Mechatronic Engineering from IF Sudeste MG — Juiz de Fora. Former PET-Physics scholar, active in scientific initiation, teaching, extension, research and innovation. Undergraduate work focused on embedded systems and 3D-printing prototyping; master's research applied Fuzzy Logic to indoor environment classification via RF signals. Joined the ATLAS-Brazil collaboration at CERN (Geneva), contributing to FPGA and electronic-system maintenance and upgrades and to new AI-model research. Currently part of a new ATLAS working group applying AI models to electron and photon triggers in the HLT (High-Level Trigger). Also holds an incomplete degree in Physics, complementing a multidisciplinary training.

name: Clethie Sediacias Bisseyou Ngatsono
bio: B.Sc. student in Electrical Engineering (Telecommunications) at UFJF since 2020. Born in the Republic of the Congo, with a solid background in mathematics. Takes part in the research and development project 'Functional Extension and Experimental Evaluation of the SAPHO Autoscalable Processor for Embedded FPGA Applications', with a paper in High Performance Computing at the XXIX National Meeting on Computational Modelling (ENMC). Also active in extension projects on circular economy and digital inclusion, reconditioning TV boxes for public schools. Holds certifications in Open RAN network architecture (CPqD/TIP Academy) and in cybersecurity (Cisco CiberEducação Marathon with Senac).

name: Mateus Hufnagel Maranha de Faria
title: Me.
bio: Master in Electrical Engineering — Electronic Systems from UFJF, with a project on digital signal processing and FPGA electronic instrumentation applied to the ATLAS tile hadronic calorimeter (LHC/CERN). Graduated in Control and Automation Engineering from CEFET-MG, Leopoldina. Substitute professor in Automation and Microprocessor Systems at CEFET-MG Leopoldina, working mainly in automation laboratory and PLC activities. Served as Junior Electrical Maintenance Specialist at Smurfit Kappa do Brasil, promoted to Specialist II in 2019, executing electrical and PLC automation projects, maintenance management and retrofit commissioning. Currently a Ph.D. student in Electrical Engineering at UFJF, linked to the High-Energy Experimental Physics and Associated Technologies group (UFJF/CERN) and LAPTEL/UFJF, working on energy reconstruction of the hadronic calorimeter.

name: Nelson Cevidanes Nascimento de Assis
title: Me.
bio: Master in Telecommunications Engineering from UFF and currently a PhD candidate in Electrical Engineering from UFJF, working at the intersection between programming, electronic engineering and High Energy Physics. My current research covers Instrumentation, Calorimetry, digital signal processing and FPGA implementation. He has experience in developing computational intelligence algorithms, data analysis in Python/R and modeling optical sensor networks. With a consolidated trajectory in the management of technological projects and entrepreneurship in energy systems (Projeta Energias Renováveis), I apply my expertise to develop analytical instrumentation and control electronics solutions aimed at particle accelerators and highly complex environments.

name: Kinn Belarmino Batista Dias
bio: Graduated in Electrical Engineering with a degree in Robotics and Industrial Automation from the Federal University of Juiz de Fora. His main area of ​​training is the fields of embedded signal processing in environments with a high rate of events and high energy physics.

name: Felipe Augusto de Oliveira França
bio: B.Sc. student in Electrical Engineering (Electronic Systems) at UFJF since 2021. He joined NIPS-CERN in September 2026 to work on HITS, the FPGA simulator of the TileCal readout chain, with Fábio Luna.

name: Thiago Campos Acácio Paschoalin
title: Prof. Me. Dr.
bio: EBTT Professor at CEFET-MG, Leopoldina Unit (Department of Electronics), and researcher at CERN on the ATLAS experiment. Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering — Electronic Systems, with emphasis on signal processing, partially developed at CERN. Master's and B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering from UFJF. Specialist in digital signal processing on FPGA devices, especially for Nuclear Instrumentation. Served three full years as a soldier in the Brazilian Navy Corps of Engineers. Experienced with FPGA devices and microcontroller programming. Worked on the PD project for the modem and PLC concentrator for the electrical grid — the 1st Brazilian broadband PLC system for LV networks.

name: Dênis Magno Carvalho de Oliveira
bio: B.Sc. student in Electrical Engineering (Electronic Systems) at UFJF since 2020, with interests in analog and digital electronics, embedded systems, programming and automation. Completed secondary education at the Colégio de Aplicação of the Federal University of Viçosa (CAP-COLUNI, 2019). He joined NIPS-CERN in September 2026 to work on SAPHO.
awards: Silver Medal — Brazilian Mathematics Olympiad OBMEP (2019)
Gold Medal, Minas Gerais state ranking — OIMSF, Rede POC and Académie de Strasbourg (2018)
Gold Medal — Brazilian Mathematics Olympiad OBMEP (2014, 2016)
Bronze Medal — Brazilian Mathematics Olympiad OBMEP (2013, 2015)

name: Carlos Eduardo da Costa Oliveira
bio: B.Sc. student in Electrical Engineering (Electronic Systems) at UFJF since 2021, with a preference for hardware and previous experience in Verilog and VHDL. He joined NIPS-CERN in September 2026 to work on HITS, the FPGA simulator of the TileCal readout chain.

name: Eder Barboza Kapisch
title: Prof. Dr.
bio: Adjunct Professor in the Department of Electrical Circuits of the Faculty of Engineering at UFJF since 2019. B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering from UFJF (2013); M.Sc. in Electrical Engineering from UFJF (2015), in the Signal Processing research line, as a CNPq fellow; sandwich doctorate through the CAPES PDSE programme at Eindhoven University of Technology (2017 to 2018); and Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from UFJF (2019), focused on digital signal processing algorithms for power quality on FPGA platforms. At NIPS-CERN he co-advises Leon Millani and Heitor Balthazar in the UFJF BIC/VIC 2026-2027 project on the impact of phase deviation on online energy reconstruction by pseudoinverse deconvolution for the ATLAS liquid-argon calorimeter.
bio_pt: Professor adjunto do Departamento de Circuitos Elétricos da Faculdade de Engenharia da UFJF desde 2019. Graduação em Engenharia Elétrica pela UFJF (2013); mestrado em Engenharia Elétrica pela UFJF (2015), na linha de processamento de sinais, como bolsista do CNPq; doutorado-sanduíche pelo PDSE da CAPES na Universidade Técnica de Eindhoven (2017 a 2018); e doutorado em Engenharia Elétrica pela UFJF (2019), sobre algoritmos de processamento digital de sinais para qualidade de energia em plataformas FPGA. No NIPS-CERN coorienta Leon Millani e Heitor Balthazar no projeto BIC/VIC 2026-2027 da UFJF sobre o impacto do desvio de fase na reconstrução online de energia por deconvolução com pseudoinversa no calorímetro de argônio líquido do ATLAS.

name: Tiago Motta Quirino
title: Prof. Dr.
bio: Adjunct Professor of Electrical Engineering at the Faculty of Engineering (FEN) of the Rio de Janeiro State University (UERJ). B.Sc. in Electrical Engineering, with emphasis on electronic systems, and M.Sc. in Electronic Engineering in the intelligent systems line, both from UERJ; Ph.D. in Electronic Engineering from UFJF. A member of the ATLAS experiment at the CERN LHC, he works on signal processing and electronic instrumentation, with a focus on technological innovation and on teaching as a way of building skills.
bio_pt: Professor adjunto de engenharia elétrica na Faculdade de Engenharia (FEN) da UERJ. Graduou-se em engenharia elétrica, com ênfase em sistemas eletrônicos, e fez mestrado em engenharia eletrônica na linha de sistemas inteligentes, ambos na UERJ; o doutorado em engenharia eletrônica é da UFJF. Membro do experimento ATLAS, no LHC do CERN, trabalha com processamento de sinais e instrumentação eletrônica, com foco na inovação tecnológica e no ensino como caminho para formar competências.

name: Gustavo Barbosa Libotte
title: Prof. Dr.
bio: Adjunct Professor in the Department of Computational Modelling of the Polytechnic Institute of the Rio de Janeiro State University (IPRJ/UERJ) and permanent member of its graduate programme in Computational Modelling. B.Sc. in Computer Engineering (2014), M.Sc. (2015) and Ph.D. (2020) in Computational Modelling, all from UERJ, followed by postdoctoral fellowships of the CNPq institutional programme at the National Laboratory for Scientific Computing (2020 to 2021) and at UFRJ (2021 to 2022). A member of the ATLAS experiment at the CERN LHC since 2023 and a full signing member of the collaboration since 2025. He sits on the editorial board of Scientific Reports and Scientific Reviews (Springer Nature) and of Vetor, and has served as a CAPES consultant in the evaluation of new graduate programmes (2024) and in the 2021 to 2024 quadrennial evaluation (2025). His work is in computational intelligence, signal processing, parameter estimation, numerical analysis and stochastic optimisation.
bio_pt: Professor adjunto do Departamento de Modelagem Computacional do Instituto Politécnico da UERJ (IPRJ/UERJ) e docente permanente do programa de pós-graduação em Modelagem Computacional. Graduação em Engenharia de Computação (2014), mestrado (2015) e doutorado (2020) em Modelagem Computacional pela UERJ, seguidos de pós-doutorado pelo programa de capacitação institucional do CNPq no Laboratório Nacional de Computação Científica (2020 a 2021) e na UFRJ (2021 a 2022). Membro do experimento ATLAS, no LHC do CERN, desde 2023, e membro signatário pleno da colaboração desde 2025. Integra o corpo editorial dos periódicos Scientific Reports e Scientific Reviews (Springer Nature) e Vetor, e foi consultor da CAPES na avaliação de propostas de cursos novos (2024) e na avaliação quadrienal de 2021 a 2024 (2025). Trabalha com inteligência computacional, processamento de sinais, estimação de parâmetros, análise numérica e otimização estocástica.

name: Bernardo Sotto-Maior Peralva
title: Prof. Dr.
bio: Associate Professor in the Department of Computational Modelling of the Polytechnic Institute of the Rio de Janeiro State University (IPRJ/UERJ) and permanent member of its graduate programme in Computational Modelling. B.Sc. (2009), M.Sc. (2012) and Ph.D. (2015) in Electrical Engineering from UFJF, after a technical course in Industrial Informatics at the university's technical college (2006). A member of the ATLAS experiment at the CERN LHC since 2007, he works on calorimetry, signal filtering and data acquisition, and in 2025 he coordinated the Tile Calorimeter trigger system through the LHC Run 3 operation, on site and remotely. He holds research fellowships from UERJ (Prociencia) and FAPERJ (Jovem Cientista do Nosso Estado), and is a member of the Brazilian Society of Computational Intelligence (SBIC) and of the Brazilian Society of Automation (SBA). He advises students at undergraduate, master's and doctoral level and coordinates national and international projects in signal detection and estimation, computational intelligence, pattern recognition and high-energy calorimetry.
bio_pt: Professor associado do Departamento de Modelagem Computacional do Instituto Politécnico da UERJ (IPRJ/UERJ) e docente permanente do programa de pós-graduação em Modelagem Computacional. Graduação (2009), mestrado (2012) e doutorado (2015) em Engenharia Elétrica pela UFJF, depois do curso técnico em Informática Industrial no Colégio Técnico Universitário da mesma universidade (2006). Colaborador do experimento ATLAS, em operação no LHC do CERN, desde 2007, atua em calorimetria, filtragem de sinais e aquisição de dados, e em 2025 coordenou o sistema de trigger do calorímetro de telhas (TileCal) durante a operação do Run 3, presencialmente e a distância. É bolsista de produtividade em pesquisa da UERJ (Prociência) e do programa Jovem Cientista do Nosso Estado (FAPERJ), e membro da Sociedade Brasileira de Inteligência Computacional (SBIC) e da Sociedade Brasileira de Automática (SBA). Orienta alunos de graduação, mestrado e doutorado e coordena projetos nacionais e internacionais em detecção e estimação de sinais, inteligência computacional, reconhecimento de padrões e calorimetria de altas energias.
